s: the Harz's "witch mountain", summited by a historic steam railway
w: The Harz's highest peak has carried witch and devil folklore for centuries -- Walpurgis Night legends still put a witches' sabbath on its summit, and Goethe used it as the setting for the Walpurgisnacht scene in Faust. A rack railway (the Brockenbahn), still steam-hauled, climbs through forest and sudden fog banks to the bare, wind-scoured top.
_facts: Highest peak in the Harz mountains and of northern Germany, at 1,141 m
Long associated with Walpurgis Night witches'-sabbath folklore, referenced in Goethe's Faust
Summited by the historic, still steam-operated Brockenbahn narrow-gauge railway
Former Cold War-era listening station on the summit, then in East German restricted border territory

s: a UNESCO-listed old town of 1,300+ half-timbered houses beneath a hilltop castle
w: One of Germany's best-preserved medieval towns, with over 1,300 half-timbered buildings spanning six centuries of construction styles packed into narrow, unusually intact streets. The hilltop castle and collegiate church -- burial place of Germany's first king, Henry the Fowler -- add real historical weight to what is otherwise just extraordinarily dense, lived-in old-town fabric.
_facts: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994, cited for one of Europe's largest collections of half-timbered buildings
Over 1,300 half-timbered houses survive, spanning roughly six centuries of building styles
Hilltop Schlossberg holds the castle and the Romanesque Quedlinburg Collegiate Church
Historic seat of the early Ottonian/Holy Roman Empire; burial site of King Henry the Fowler
